what: Leg 1 of the 'does Itemator catch real problems' work, written before any comment is scored: of the human reviewers' scope comments on AI-agent pull requests in the public AIDev dataset, how often did the rules (v6, frozen) list the file the reviewer was talking about? Read-only; nothing is posted.
dataset: hao-li/AIDev on Hugging Face (arXiv 2507.15003; CC-BY-4.0; patches keep each repository's licence), read through the dataset-viewer API. Pull requests and review comments from the v4 popular-repository subset; linked issues from hao-li/AIDev-7.6M.
sample: Every inline review comment in `pr_review_comments` whose author type is User and whose text contains, ignoring case, one of: unrelated, out of scope, separate PR, not needed, unnecessary, and that sits on a file path. The list of comment ids is eval/aidev_recall_cases.json (written by eval/aidev_cases.py before any scoring). Nobody read any comment text to build it.
files: the pull request's files as they stood up to and including the commit the comment was first made on (`original_commit_id`): per-commit file rows in commit order; a file added and later removed vanishes; patches of several commits are joined in order. A comment whose commit is not among the pull request's commits is 'unreadable' and counted apart.
task: the linked issue's title and text when the 7.6M copy links one; otherwise the pull request's title and text (reported apart). A second run uses the title alone, to see whether the agent's own description excuses its extras.
rules: itemator.extras.analyse, rules version 6 (frozen), with the repository name
hit: an extra whose path (or a file in its list, or a listed directory that holds it) is the commented file
kinds: listable_kind in eval/aidev_recall.py decides, from the path alone, whether the file is of a kind the rules can list (dependency manifest, CI or config, agent instructions, generated, binary); everything else is source, tests or docs

outcome.primary: among comments on a file of a listable kind, the share whose file the rules listed (counts and a Wilson 95% interval)
also_reported: the same share over all comments
by agent, by pull request state (merged, closed, open), by where the task text came from
the number of pull requests with at least one listed comment
the title-only run for both shares

reading_rule: Report the primary share first, in plain words, with its counts. The share over all comments is reported beside it, never instead. No 'catches X percent of scope creep' sentence is written from either number. Any of K1's documented cases that also appear in the sample are marked and reported apart.
published: Comment ids, pull request addresses, file paths, kinds and yes/no results. No comment text, no patch text.
limits: A reviewer's phrase is not a verdict that the file did not belong. Concatenated per-commit patches are an approximation of the pull request at that moment. The dataset is a snapshot of popular repositories. The rules compare a change with its task; a vague pull request text can hide an extra (the title-only run measures this). One run of frozen rules; nothing here was tuned on these comments.
seen_before_registration: Only counts from the fleet-9 research agent K2: 710 human comments on 477 pull requests, of which 63 sit on a file of a listable kind by path (CI or config 38, dependency 13, agent instructions 7, binary 3, generated 2), and that about half the pull requests have a linked issue. No comment was scored. Separately, on 2026-10-16 I ran the v6 rules on five documented cases from K1 (listed the objected-to change in none); those are the development set for any later rules version and are not part of this sample unless they appear in it.
